notes.text: Manali test summary.

notes.label: Overview
notes.text: Manali, at about 2,050 m in the Beas valley, takes its name from 'Manu-Alaya', the abode of the sage Manu, and is often called the 'Valley of the Gods'. Its best-known shrine is the Hadimba Devi Temple of 1553, in a cedar forest above town; Old Manali has the Manu Temple and relaxed cafés, and Vashisht's hot springs are 3 km away.

notes.label: Overview
notes.text: Manali is also the region's adventure base: skiing and paragliding at Solang Valley, 13 km away; the Hampta Pass trek; and the high road to Rohtang Pass, 51 km away, which needs a permit. The 9.02-km Atal Tunnel, opened in 2020, runs beneath the pass to Lahaul.

notes.text: Visit the Hadimba Devi Temple and the nearby Museum of Himachal Culture & Folk Art.

notes.label: Best time to visit
notes.text: Manali has two main visitor seasons: April to July, when summer days are around 22–30°C, and October to December. Snow falls mainly from December to early March, and in December–January it can drop below −5°C — the time for skiing at Solang and the Winter Carnival in the first week of January.

notes.label: Best time to visit
notes.text: The road over Rohtang Pass usually reopens around May and closes in late November; June to August is when visitors drive up to see snow. In the monsoon (July–August) roads can be hit by landslides, and paragliding and rafting stop from 15 July to 15 September. For Solang, Incredible India suggests April to June and September to January.

notes.label: How to reach
notes.text: By air: Kullu–Manali airport at Bhuntar is 50 km from Manali, with taxis and buses onward. Flights connect it with Delhi (about 1.5 hours), Chandigarh and Shimla.

notes.label: How to reach
notes.text: By bus: Delhi is about 550 km away. Deluxe and AC Volvo buses run regularly from Delhi, Chandigarh, Shimla, Dharamshala and other cities — book ahead. HRTC, HPTDC and private operators run services.

notes.label: How to reach
notes.text: By train: there is no railway to Manali. The nearest railheads are Joginder Nagar, on the narrow-gauge line from Pathankot, and Kiratpur, about 200 km from Kullu on the Chandigarh highway; continue by road.

notes.label: How to reach
notes.text: By car: vehicles not registered in Himachal pay a green tax to enter Manali (₹200 for a car), bought online and valid for seven days.

notes.label: Local transport
notes.text: Taxis wait at Manali's local taxi stand. Hire only authorised taxis from registered operators or taxi unions and ask for the government-approved fare chart; HPTDC also runs its own coaches and taxis. HRTC buses leave from the Manali bus stand for major cities.

notes.label: Local transport
notes.text: On foot, Vashisht is linked to the market by a paved path, and the Manu Temple in Old Manali is within walking distance, about 3 km from the main bazaar.

notes.label: Local transport
notes.text: Driving yourself: vehicles not registered in Himachal pay a green tax on entering Manali, and the road to Rohtang Pass needs a separate online permit. Park at the car park near the main market.

notes.label: Travel tips
notes.text: Apply for a Rohtang permit when the online quota opens at 10:00 or 16:00, up to two days ahead.

notes.label: Travel tips
notes.text: Book AC or Volvo buses from Delhi in advance.

notes.label: Travel tips
notes.text: Carry warm layers even in summer for Solang and Rohtang.

notes.label: Travel tips
notes.text: Ask taxi drivers for the government-approved fare chart.

notes.label: FAQs
notes.title: Do I need a permit for Rohtang Pass?
notes.text: Yes. Tourist vehicles need an online permit — ₹500 per vehicle plus a ₹50 congestion charge — applied for up to two days ahead against a daily quota. Carry a printout.

notes.label: FAQs
notes.title: When does it snow in Manali?
notes.text: Mainly from December to early March. In December–January temperatures can drop below −5°C.

notes.label: FAQs
notes.title: Is Rohtang Pass open in winter?
notes.text: No. Heavy snow closes it in late November and it reopens around May. The Atal Tunnel, which bypasses the pass, connects Manali with Lahaul.

notes.label: FAQs
notes.title: How far is the airport?
notes.text: Kullu–Manali airport at Bhuntar is 50 km from Manali, with flights from Delhi (about 1.5 hours), Chandigarh and Shimla.

notes.label: FAQs
notes.title: Is there a train to Manali?
notes.text: No. The nearest railheads are Joginder Nagar (narrow gauge, via Pathankot) and Kiratpur; continue by road.

notes.label: FAQs
notes.title: Can I go paragliding in August?
notes.text: No — paragliding, rafting and river crossing are closed every monsoon from 15 July to 15 September.

notes.label: FAQs
notes.title: Do cars from other states pay a tax?
notes.text: Yes. Vehicles not registered in Himachal pay a green tax to enter Manali (₹200 for a car), valid for seven days.

notes.label: FAQs
notes.title: How many days do I need?
notes.text: Three days covers the town, Solang and one high-road day; four lets you add Naggar; seven adds Vashisht's waterfall walk, Kullu and slower days.

notes.label: Where to stay
notes.text: Mall Road and the main market are the most convenient base: the Mall's shops and restaurants are on your doorstep and there is a public car park near the market. Old Manali, up the hill, has narrow lanes and cafés popular with foreign travellers. Vashisht, across the Beas and more compact than Old Manali, has rooftop cafés with mountain views and the hot springs.

notes.label: Where to stay
notes.text: Wherever you stay, choose hotels, guest houses or homestays registered with the Department of Tourism.

notes.title: Visas
notes.text: Apply for an e-Tourist visa at least 4 days before arrival; your passport needs at least six months' validity.

notes.label: Practical information
notes.title: Payments
notes.text: Visitors can pay by QR code with NPCI's UPI One World wallet after a passport-and-visa KYC check. Carry some cash for small purchases.

notes.label: Practical information
notes.title: Emergency
notes.text: Dial 112 for police, fire or ambulance, or 108 for the free ambulance service.

notes.label: Practical information
notes.title: Rohtang permits
notes.text: ₹500 per vehicle plus a ₹50 congestion charge (₹100 for buses), online, up to two days ahead, against a daily quota of 800 petrol and 400 diesel vehicles. Vehicles must be no more than 10 years old; carry a printout.

notes.label: Practical information
notes.title: Green tax
notes.text: Vehicles not registered in Himachal pay ₹100 (bike), ₹200 (car), ₹300 (passenger vehicle) or ₹500 (goods vehicle) to enter Manali; valid seven days.

notes.label: Safety and health
notes.title: Emergency numbers
notes.text: 112 for police, fire or ambulance; 108 for the free 24x7 ambulance.

notes.label: Safety and health
notes.title: Weather and altitude
notes.text: Weather changes fast; Rohtang Pass is notorious for sudden snowstorms, so check the forecast and turn back if it closes in.

notes.label: Safety and health
notes.title: Monsoon
notes.text: July–August brings landslides and rock-falls; paragliding, rafting and river crossing are closed from 15 July to 15 September.

notes.label: Safety and health
notes.title: Rivers
notes.text: The Beas is fast and deceptive — don't stand on riverside boulders for photos.

notes.label: Safety and health
notes.title: Adventure operators
notes.text: Book only government-authorised, licensed operators; joy-ride rafting is allowed only up to Class II rapids.

notes.label: Safety and health
notes.title: Treks
notes.text: Inform the local authorities before a high-altitude trek and hire registered guides and porters.

notes.label: Safety and health
notes.title: Drugs
notes.text: Carrying or using cannabis or other drugs is a crime under the NDPS Act, punishable with imprisonment.

notes.label: Activity
notes.title: Bathe in the Vashisht hot springs
notes.text: Sulphurous hot-spring baths with separate areas for women and men, 3 km from Manali.

notes.label: Bathe in the Vashisht hot springs · Overview
notes.text: Vashisht's sulphurous hot springs feed a walled stone pool and separate shower rooms for women and men, with hot and cold water piped in. Charges are nominal, and the baths are listed as open 7 am–1 pm and 2 pm–9 pm daily. Walk there on the paved path from Manali market.

notes.label: Activity
notes.title: Himachal Tourism Club House
notes.text: Go-karting, roller skating, billiards and river crossing beside the Manalsu stream.

notes.label: Himachal Tourism Club House · Overview
notes.text: Run by Himachal Tourism on the left bank of the Manalsu stream, a tributary of the Beas, the Club House is an activity complex with roller skating, billiards, table tennis, go-karting and river crossing — an easy family afternoon in town.

notes.label: Nature
notes.title: Jogini Falls
notes.text: A waterfall reached on foot from Vashisht village.

notes.label: Jogini Falls · Overview
notes.text: Jogini Waterfall is reached on foot from Vashisht village, on a trail that makes a refreshing short trek with mountain views. Himachal Tourism lists it among the excursions around Manali with Nehru Kund and Kothi. Combine it with a bath in the Vashisht hot springs.

notes.label: Attraction
notes.title: Manali Gompa
notes.text: The colourful Tibetan monastery near the Mall, built by refugees in the 1960s.

notes.label: Manali Gompa · Overview
notes.text: Close to the Mall, the Gadhan Thekchhokling Gompa greets you with bright colours: a large Buddha statue at the entrance, freshly painted façades, lawns and murals of the Buddha's life. It was built by Tibetan refugees in the early 1960s; visit in the morning or evening for prayers.

notes.label: Nature
notes.title: Manali Wildlife Sanctuary
notes.text: Deodar and walnut forest above Dhungri, home to monal, musk deer and brown bear.

notes.label: Manali Wildlife Sanctuary · Overview
notes.text: The sanctuary starts about 2 km from Manali. A bridle path past the Dhungri temple leads through dense deodar, kail, walnut and maple forest towards the alpine grassland of Gallant thatch; monal, musk deer and brown bear may be seen. It covers about 31.8 sq km.

notes.label: Activity
notes.title: Manali Winter Carnival
notes.text: A week of folk dance, parades and a ski competition in the first week of January.

notes.label: Manali Winter Carnival · Overview
notes.text: Held in the first week of January every year, Manali's week-long Winter Carnival brings folk-dance troupes from several states, a carnival parade, singing and dance competitions and a Winter Queen contest. A ski competition is held nearby at Solang Valley.

notes.label: Activity
notes.title: Mountaineering and adventure courses
notes.text: Basic to advanced courses at Manali's Atal Bihari Vajpayee Institute of Mountaineering.

notes.label: Mountaineering and adventure courses · Overview
notes.text: The Atal Bihari Vajpayee Institute of Mountaineering and Allied Sports, founded in Manali in 1961, runs basic to advanced courses in mountaineering, rock climbing, trekking, river rafting, paragliding and other adventure sports. Solang Valley is a base camp for expeditions to Anjani Mahadev, Hanuman Tibba and Patalsu.

notes.label: Museum
notes.title: Museum of Himachal Culture & Folk Art
notes.text: A small museum of local artefacts and costume near the Hadimba Temple.

notes.label: Museum of Himachal Culture & Folk Art · Overview
notes.text: This small museum near the Hadimba Devi Temple offers a glimpse of Himachal's cultural heritage, with traditional artefacts, musical instruments, clothing and household items that show the daily life and customs of the region. Opening hours and fees could not be confirmed from an official source.

notes.label: Nature
notes.title: Nehru Kund
notes.text: A clear spring fed by Bhrigu Lake on the Manali–Leh highway, about 5–6 km from Manali.

notes.label: Nehru Kund · Overview
notes.text: On the Manali–Leh highway, about 5–6 km from Manali towards Rohtang, Nehru Kund is a natural spring fed by Bhrigu Lake. It is named after India's first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, who is said to have drunk only from this spring on his visits to Manali.

notes.label: Activity
notes.title: Old Manali and Vashisht cafés
notes.text: Western menus in Old Manali's lanes and rooftop cafés with views in Vashisht.

notes.label: Old Manali and Vashisht cafés · Overview
notes.text: Old Manali, up a path beyond the town, has narrow streets, many foreign travellers and cafés where most menus are Western. Vashisht, more compact, is known for rooftop eateries with mountain views serving Italian, Mexican and Israeli dishes. For North Indian food, head to Mall Road.

notes.label: Activity
notes.title: Shopping on Mall Road
notes.text: Woollens, Kullu shawls, Himachali caps and handicrafts on the Mall and in the markets.

notes.label: Shopping on Mall Road · Overview
notes.text: Mall Road and the bazaar have outlets for souvenirs, woollens and Himachali handloom and handicrafts, and the Tibetan market, Manu Market and the Himachal Emporium are well worth exploring. Look for Kullu shawls, Himachali caps and handcrafted wooden items; government emporiums have reasonable prices and assured quality.

notes.label: Attraction
notes.title: Vashisht
notes.text: A village 3 km from Manali with sulphurous hot springs and a Kath Kuni temple.

notes.label: Vashisht · Overview
notes.text: Across the Beas, 3 km from Manali and linked to the market by a paved path, the village of Vashisht is known for its sulphurous hot springs and its Kath Kuni-style temple of Sage Vashisht. The baths have a walled stone pool and separate shower rooms for women and men with hot and cold water piped in; charges are nominal, and they are listed as open 7 am–1 pm and 2 pm–9 pm daily. Vashisht is also known for rooftop cafés with mountain views, and a trail leads on to Jogini Waterfall.

notes.label: Attraction
notes.title: Atal Tunnel
notes.text: The 9.02-km highway tunnel under the Rohtang Pass, linking Manali with Lahaul in about 2 hours instead of 5–6.

notes.label: Trek
notes.title: Bhrigu Lake trek
notes.text: A high meadow trek to a sacred glacial lake at about 4,235 m, starting from Gulaba on the Rohtang road.

notes.label: Temple
notes.title: Hadimba Temple
notes.text: Hadimba Temple is an easy Manali visit, about 2 km from Mall Road, with a cool cedar forest around it. Go before 9:00 AM for quieter darshan and wear shoes you can remove easily.

notes.label: Trek
notes.title: Hampta Pass trek
notes.text: A 4-day crossing at 4,270 m from the green Kullu valley into the stark Chandra valley of Lahaul.

notes.label: Temple
notes.title: Manu Temple
notes.text: The stone-and-wood temple in Old Manali dedicated to the sage Manu, from whom Manali takes its name.

notes.label: Viewpoint
notes.title: Rohtang Pass
notes.text: The 3,978-m pass between the Kullu valley and Lahaul, open roughly May to November, with the Atal Tunnel beneath it.

notes.label: Nature
notes.title: Solang Valley
notes.text: Manali's playground: skiing in winter, paragliding and a ropeway in summer.

notes.title: Jagatsukh

notes.label: Town
notes.title: Naggar
notes.text: A village above the Beas with a 15th-century castle, old temples and the Roerich gallery.

notes.label: Things to do

notes.text: White-water rafting on the snow-fed Beas between Manali and Kullu — summer only, closed 15 July to 15 September.

notes.label: Things to do

notes.text: Winter skiing on Solang's slopes, for beginners and experts, with courses at Manali's mountaineering institute.

notes.label: 3-day itinerary
notes.title: Manali in 3 days
notes.text: The Hadimba Temple, Old Manali and the gompa; a day at Solang; and a high-road day through the Atal Tunnel to Sissu or up to Rohtang with a permit. Stops include Hadimba Devi Temple, Museum of Himachal Culture & Folk Art, Old Manali and the Manu Temple, Manali Gompa and Mall Road.

notes.label: 4-day itinerary
notes.title: Manali in 4 days
notes.text: The Hadimba Temple and Old Manali, a day at Solang, the high road to Rohtang (with a permit) or the Atal Tunnel, and Naggar and Vashisht's hot springs. Stops include Hadimba Devi Temple, Museum of Himachal Culture & Folk Art, Old Manali and the Manu Temple, Manali Gompa and Mall Road.

notes.label: 7-day itinerary
notes.title: Manali in 7 days
notes.text: A slow week: Manali's temples and cafés, Vashisht and Jogini Falls, Solang, a high-road day, Naggar and Jagatsukh, and Kullu on the way out. Stops include Arrive from Bhuntar airport or by bus, Mall Road and the gompa, Hadimba Devi Temple, Museum of Himachal Culture & Folk Art.
